Tamro (a Nordic healthcare and pharmaceutical logistics company owned by PHOENIX group)
does not manufacture continuous glucose monitors, smartwatches, or wearable ECGs
; instead, they provide
Tamro Care Services
like the Smila automated medicine dispenser for remote patient support at home. General smartwatches and wearable trackers attempt non-invasive blood glucose or ECG via wrist sensors, but true medical remote monitoring relies on dedicated certified devices.
Amazon.in
Wearable Health Tech Options
Continuous Glucose Monitors (CGMs):
Real-time subcutaneous sensors like Abbott FreeStyle Libre or Dexcom pierce the skin to track interstitial glucose levels continuously, distinct from wrist wearables.
Smartwatches & Wearable ECG:
Devices like the Apple Watch or Samsung Galaxy Watch offer spot-check ECGs and optical heart rate (PPG) tracking, though non-invasive wrist glucose tracking remains experimental and unverified for clinical diabetes management.
Amazon.in
Sleep Trackers:
Dedicated rings (like Oura) or band monitors use photoplethysmography and accelerometers to measure sleep stages, HRV, and skin temperature.
Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM):
Clinical setups use cellular or Bluetooth-enabled blood pressure cuffs, pulse oximeters, and weight scales to transmit patient vitals directly to healthcare providers.
